extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (and patent examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing and prosecuting continuation, divisional, and continuation-in-part patent applications (including oath/declaration, specification/drawings, incorporation by reference, filing date, and inventorship rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date — new matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An incorporation by reference statement added after an application's filing date is not effective because no new matter can be added after filing (see 35 U.S.C. 132(a)). If material needed for a filing date is incorporated by reference, a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) or 1.182 may be required; until granted the application will not be entitled to a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements (pre- and post- Dec 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before December 18, 2013 (under 37 CFR 1.53(b)), a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 containing a description pursuant to 37 CFR 1.71 and at least one claim pursuant to 37 CFR 1.75, and any drawing required by 37 CFR 1.81(a) were required for a filing date. For nonprovisional applications filed on or after December 18, 2013 (other than design patents), the filing date is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received; utility and plant applications no longer required at least one claim or drawings to receive a filing date. A design patent application’s filing date still requires a specification including at least one claim and any required drawings (35 U.S.C. 171(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 601.01(a). Also, a nonprovisional filed under 35 U.S.C.111(a) on/after Dec 18, 2013 may be filed by reference to a previously filed application indicating the specification and any drawings are replaced by that reference (see MPEP § 601.01(a), subsection III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types/conditions for continuation/divisional/CIP filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuing application (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part) may be filed under conditions specified in 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) and 37 CFR 1.78(c) and (d). A continuation or divisional that names the same or fewer inventors than the prior application may be filed under one paragraph; a continuation-in-part or a continuation/divisional naming an inventor not named in the prior application must be filed under a different paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to clearly designate the application relationship (continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part) by submitting a reference to the prior-filed application with the appropriate relationship in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2) (e.g., in an application data sheet for filings on/after Sept 16, 2012, or in the first sentence(s) of the specification for earlier filings) to avoid petitions and incorrect filing-receipt indications. See MPEP § 211 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of continuing application relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless an application is submitted with a statement that it is a continuation or divisional application, the Office will process it as a new non-continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate continuation/divisional/CIP status by including a reference to the prior-filed application with the appropriate relationship in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78(d)(2) (application data sheet or first sentence(s) of the specification), to avoid petitions under 37 CFR 1.78(e) and associated fees (37 CFR 1.17(m)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and oath/declaration timing for complete application
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, application size fee, and the inventor’s oath or declaration (in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 or substitute under 1.64 where applicable) are required by 37 CFR 1.51(b) for a complete application; these may be filed after the filing date upon payment of the surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(f). For applications filed prior to Sept 16, 2012, the statutory filing fee and an oath or declaration were required but may be filed after the filing date upon payment of surcharge (see 37 CFR 1.53(f) and MPEP § 607).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing receipt consequences may vary; where an application contains an ADS identifying each inventor and mailing address, the oath/declaration may be postponed until payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of copy of prior oath/declaration in continuing applications (post-Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath/declaration is not required for an inventor in a continuing application that claims the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) if an oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 (or substitute under 1.64) was executed and filed in the earlier-filed application and a copy showing the signature or indication of execution is submitted in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy of the prior oath/declaration submitted must comply with 35 U.S.C. 115 and 37 CFR 1.63 (as revised effective Sept 16, 2012) when the continuing application is filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 (e.g., must state inventor is original inventor and authorized the filing; must include 18 U.S.C.1001 acknowledgement). See MPEP § 602.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship determination in continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of a continuing application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is the inventor(s) specified in the application data sheet filed before or concurrently with the copy of the inventor’s oath/declaration from the earlier-filed application; if no ADS is filed, inventorship is as set forth in the copy of the prior oath/declaration unless accompanied by a signed 37 CFR 1.33(b) statement stating the names of each inventor in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new joint inventor named in the continuing application must provide an oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63, except as provided in 37 CFR 1.64.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA conditions for using copy of oath/declaration in continuation/divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of an executed oath/declaration from a prior application may be used in a continuation/divisional if: (i) the prior application contained an oath/declaration as prescribed, (ii) the continuation/divisional is filed by all or fewer than all inventors named in the prior application, (iii) the specification and drawings filed contain no matter that would have been new matter in the prior application, and (iv) a copy of the executed oath/declaration showing signature or indication of signing is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy submitted must be accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the name(s) of person(s) who are not inventors in the continuation/divisional. If the prior application had 37 CFR 1.47 status, additional documentary requirements (copy of decision granting 1.47 status) apply. See pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.63(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file new oath/declaration when new inventor added
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed oath or declaration must be filed in a continuation or divisional application naming an inventor not named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies both pre- and post-AIA as specified: post-Sept 16, 2012 certain copies may be acceptable only if they comply with revised 35 U.S.C.115 / 37 CFR 1.63; for pre-Sept 16, 2012 filings the newly executed oath is required when a new inventor is named in a continuation/divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and drawings — no new matter allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application may be filed with a new specification and drawings or a new specification/drawings with a newly executed or copied oath/declaration provided the new specification and drawings do not contain any subject matter that would have been new matter in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is responsible to review any new specification or drawings for a continuation/divisional application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) to determine they contain no new matter. If the examiner determines the continuing application contains new matter relative to the prior application, the examiner should notify applicant in the next Office action and indicate the application should be redesignated as a continuation-in-part. If new matter exists, applicant is required to delete the benefit claim or change the relationship to continuation-in-part (Form paragraph 2.10.01 may be used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims submission practice in continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that applicants file a new set of claims as the original claims of the continuing application rather than filing a copy of the claims from the prior application and a preliminary amendment to those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) with a preliminary amendment making desired changes to specification or claims is NOT recommended because for applications filed on/after Sept 21, 2004 a preliminary amendment present on the filing date is part of the original disclosure; problematic amendment formats may trigger notices from OPAP requiring resubmission in a publishable format (see 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1) and 1.215). To have a patent application publication contain only a desired set of claims, file a continuation/divisional under 37 CFR 1.53(b) with a new specification containing only the desired set of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and provisional rights consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any utility or plant patent application that will be published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b) should be filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) with a specification that includes any claim(s) and drawings that the applicant would like to have published, because under 35 U.S.C. 154(d) a patentee may obtain provisional rights if the invention claimed in the patent is substantially identical to the invention claimed in the application publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that preliminary amendments present on filing may become part of the original disclosure for publication; ensure any amendment is in a format usable for publication (substitute specification per 37 CFR 1.121(b)(3) and 1.125).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — explicit statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may incorporate by reference the prior application by the continuing application-as-filed, by an explicit statement in the specification that such prior application(s) are 'hereby incorporated by reference.' The statement must appear in the specification (see 37 CFR 1.57(c) and MPEP § 608.01(p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of this incorporation by reference permits applicant to amend the continuing application to include subject matter from the prior application(s) without the need for a petition provided the continuing application is entitled to a filing date notwithstanding the incorporation by reference. Mere reference to another application, patent, or publication is not an incorporation for purposes of the disclosure required by 35 U.S.C.112(a) (In re de Seversky). For apps filed on/after Sept 21, 2004 a claim for benefit under 37 CFR 1.78 present on the filing date is considered an incorporation by reference as to inadvertently omitted material subject to 37 CFR 1.57(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference added after filing date is ineffective
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference statement added after an application’s filing date is not effective because no new matter can be added after the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an incorporation by reference statement is included in an amendment to the specification to add a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 after the filing date, the amendment would not be proper (Dart Indus. v. Banner). When a benefit claim is submitted after filing, the reference to the prior application cannot include an incorporation by reference statement of the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to accord filing date when material omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If material needed to accord an application a filing date is completely contained within a prior-filed application to which benefit is claimed, applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with the required fee and an amendment with the inadvertently omitted material requesting entry of the amendment and that the application be accorded a filing date as of the original deposit date. Alternatively, a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee and amendment may be used when an explicit incorporation by reference statement is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until such a petition is granted, the application will not be entitled to a filing date. An amendment submitting omitted material relying on incorporation by reference will not be entered unless a decision granting the petition states the application is accorded a filing date and the amendment will be entered. See 37 CFR 1.57(b)(3) and MPEP § 217.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an application entitled to a filing date may add omitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: If a continuing application as originally filed is entitled to a filing date despite inadvertent omission of a portion of the prior application(s), applicant may be permitted to add the omitted material by way of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.57(b), provided the amendment is made within any time period set by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an originally filed application included a proper explicit incorporation by reference statement (or one made effective under 37 CFR 1.57(h)), omitted pages/figures may be added by amendment provided the omitted item(s) contains only subject matter in common with the properly incorporated document. If OPAP identified omitted items in a 'Notice of Omitted Item(s)', applicant must respond by filing an appropriate amendment. See MPEP §§ 601.01(d), 601.01(g), and § 217.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration content requirements (post-Sept 16, 2012 / 35 U.S.C.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuing applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 a copy of the inventor’s oath/declaration from an earlier-filed application submitted in the continuing application must comply with the requirements of 35 U.S.C.115 and 37 CFR 1.63 (or 1.64). For example, the inventor’s oath/declaration must include a statement that the inventor is an original inventor of the claimed application and authorized the filing, and must acknowledge that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 by fine or imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accordingly, a new inventor’s oath/declaration may need to be filed in a continuing application filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 where the prior application was filed before Sept 16, 2012. See MPEP § 602.05(a) for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement use (37 CFR 1.64)
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 is not required for an inventor in a continuing application that claims the benefit of an earlier-filed application provided a substitute statement under 1.64 was executed and filed in the earlier-filed application and a copy showing execution is submitted in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With respect to an application naming only one inventor, any reference to the inventor's oath/declaration includes a substitute statement executed under 37 CFR 1.64. For more than one inventor, references mean the collective oaths/declarations or substitute statements executed by or with respect to all joint inventors unless otherwise clear from context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 (Rule 47) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuations/divisionals filed prior to Sept 16, 2012 that contain a copy of an oath/declaration not signed by one of the inventors and a copy of the decision according 37 CFR 1.47 status in the prior application, the file should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions (and then to Technology Center). The Office of Petitions will notify applicant that 'Rule 47' status has been accorded but will not repeat notice to the nonsigning inventor or Official Gazette announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an application and a copy of the prior oath/declaration are filed without a statement requesting deletion of names, the continuation/divisional will be treated as naming as inventors the persons named in the copy of the executed oath/declaration from the prior application. Statements requesting deletion must be signed by persons authorized under 37 CFR 1.33(b). See MPEP § 602.01(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of power of attorney/correspondence address identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the power of attorney or correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, the change must be identified in the continuation or divisional application; otherwise the Office may not recognize the change in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, 37 CFR 1.32(d) provides that a power of attorney from a prior national application for which benefit is claimed may have effect in the continuing application if a copy of the power of attorney from the prior application is filed in the continuing application, unless certain exceptions apply (see 37 CFR 1.32(d)).
